titulo: I would like you to come
intro: After a wish or request in the conditional, the verb goes in the imperfect subjunctive.
p.me gustaría que.consejo: It sounds softer than «quiero que». The imperfect subjunctive follows: «me gustaría que vinieras».
p.quisiera que.consejo: «Quisiera» is already an imperfect subjunctive form of «querer». It is very polite.
p.preferiría que.consejo: The conditional «preferiría» asks for the imperfect subjunctive: «preferiría que salieras».
p.vinieras.consejo: It comes from «vinieron» dropping -ron: «viniera, vinieras…». It is not past: it is a wish.
p.hablara.consejo: It comes from «hablaron»: drop -ron and add -ra. For «nosotros» it takes an accent: «habláramos».
p.viviera.consejo: From «vivieron»: «viviera, vivieras…». The endings are the same for -ar, -er and -ir.
p.sugerencia.consejo: The g sounds h: «su-he-REN-thya». It is feminine: «una sugerencia».
p.horario.consejo: It is masculine: «el horario». «Cambiar el horario» means changing the hours.
p.turno.consejo: At work it is each person's timetable: «turno de mañana», «turno de noche».
p.avisar.consejo: The v sounds b: «a-bi-SAR». «Avísame» is the command with a pronoun.
p.con tiempo.consejo: It is a fixed expression: «avísame con tiempo» means «tell me beforehand».
b1.texto:
To ask something politely of another person, use a wish verb in the **conditional** and the **imperfect subjunctive**:

- **Me gustaría que vinieras** to lunch.
- **Quisiera que conocieras** my sister.
- **Preferiría que me avisaras** in advance.

If the subject is the **same**, use the infinitive: **me gustaría viajar**.

The imperfect subjunctive is formed from the 3rd person plural of the **preterite**: **hablaron → hablara**, **comieron → comiera**, **vivieron → viviera**. The **-se** form also exists (viniese).

Even if it looks past, here it speaks of the **present or the future**: it is a wish, not a memory.
b2.f0.texto: I would like you to come for lunch on Sunday.
b2.f1.texto: I would love to, but I work in the morning.
b2.f2.texto: I would like you to meet my sister.
b2.f3.texto: I would prefer you to let me know in advance.
b2.f4.texto: I will let you know on Friday without fail.
b2.f5.texto: I wish I could change my shift.
b2.f6.texto: I would like your boss to give you that day off.
b2.f7.texto: I am going to talk to him.
b2.f8.texto: I would really like to see you there.
b4.texto:
It is formed from the 3rd person plural of the **preterite**, dropping **-ron** and adding:

- **-ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran**: hablara, hablaras, hablara, hablá**ramos**, hablarais, hablaran.

Verbs that are irregular in the preterite keep their stem: vinieron → **viniera**, tuvieron → **tuviera**, hicieron → **hiciera**, fueron → **fuera**, dijeron → **dijera**, pudieron → **pudiera**.

It is used:

- After a wish in the conditional: **me gustaría que vinieras**.
- After a wish or request in the past: **quería que vinieras**.
- With **ojalá** for a hard-to-reach wish: **ojalá pudiera**.

The **-se** form (viniese) means the same but is used less.
b4.e0.texto: I wanted you to come earlier.
b4.e1.texto: I would like you to speak more slowly.
b4.e2.texto: I would prefer us to live nearby.
b5.f0.texto: The harbour café opens its doors before the sun comes out.
b5.f1.texto: Inés makes the coffee with quick hands and a sleepy smile.
b5.f2.texto: The steam rises in white spirals up to the lamps on the ceiling.
b5.f3.texto: Marcos wipes the wooden tables and listens to the crash of the waves.
b5.f4.texto: Outside, the boats sleep in a row on the grey water.
b5.f5.texto: At mid-morning the fishermen arrive with their boots full of salt.
b5.f6.texto: They order toasted bread, green oil and a very strong coffee.
b5.f7.texto: Inés serves them patiently and tells them the latest gossip from the harbour.
b5.f8.texto: A little girl draws coloured boats on a paper napkin.
b5.f9.texto: Marcos looks out of the window and dreams of a boat of his own.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! A wish in the conditional: imperfect subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The infinitive does not go after «que».
b6.pregunta: You politely ask another person to come. What is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: The imperfect subjunctive does not start from «yo».
b7.o2.refuerzo: The future is not the base of the subjunctive.
b8.o0.refuerzo: That would be another person. Here it is you.
b8.o2.refuerzo: «Viajaría» is conditional and here the infinitive is needed.
b8.pregunta: You are the one who travels. What is missing?
b9.frase: Preferiría que me avisaras con tiempo
b9.traduccion: I would prefer you to let me know in advance
b10.pregunta: What is the imperfect subjunctive of «tener» (tú)?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I would like you to come» (tú).
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Lleguen» is present; with «quisiera» comes the imperfect.
b12.pregunta: You ask several people to arrive earlier. What is missing?
p.conocieras.consejo: From «conocer», to know or meet. After «quisiera que», the subjunctive is used.
p.avisaras.glosa: you would let me know (avisar, subjunctive)
p.avisaras.consejo: From «avisar», to warn or inform. After «preferiría que» the subjunctive appears.
p.falta.consejo: «Sin falta» means «without fail». The «f» and the «l» are clear.
p.diera.consejo: From «dar», to give. In the subjunctive, «dar» becomes «diera».
p.verte.consejo: From «ver», with «te» at the end meaning «you». The «v» sounds like «b».
p.hablaras.consejo: From «hablar», to speak. Its subjunctive ends in -aras after «que».
p.viviéramos.consejo: From «vivir». The accent shows the stress on «é»: «bi-BYE-ra-mos».
p.rápidas.consejo: It agrees with «manos», which is feminine plural, so it ends in -as.
p.dormida.consejo: From «dormir», to sleep. It agrees with «sonrisa», a feminine noun.
p.espirales.consejo: Lines that curl round and round. It is feminine plural.
p.lámparas.consejo: Things that give light. The accent is on «LAM».
p.pescadores.consejo: People who catch fish. The «c» before «a» sounds like «k».
p.cargado.consejo: From «cargar», to load. For coffee it means strong, like a load of flavour.
p.chisme.consejo: Talk about other people's private business. The «ch» sounds like «ch» in English.
p.propio.consejo: Used when something belongs only to you, like «un barco propio».
p.tuvieras.consejo: From «tener». The subjunctive form has the stem «tuv-» with -ieras.
p.llegaran.consejo: From «llegar». The «ll» sounds like «y», and the subjunctive ends in -aran.
